title: Southern cornbread
subtitle: Unsweetened cast-iron skillet cornbread with a crisp base
excerpt: Southern cornbread is a dense, savoury bread made from coarse ground polenta (cornmeal), buttermilk, and egg, baked in a greased cast-iron skillet at a high temperature. It comes out with a crisp, golden base from the hot fat in the pan and a moist, crumbly interior. Serves alongside chilli, gumbo, or collard greens.
sourceNotes: Southern American culinary tradition. Southern cornbread is documented in Edna Lewis, The Taste of Country Cooking (1976), who describes the cast-iron skillet method and the tradition of unsweetened cornbread in the Deep South. Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, gives the original cornbread recipe.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, wrap in foil, and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat wrapped in a 180°C oven for 15 minutes.

content.text: Southern cornbread uses coarse-ground polenta (cornmeal), buttermilk, and egg, baked in a well-greased cast-iron skillet that goes into the oven hot. The hot fat in the pan creates a crisp, caramelised base the moment the batter hits it. The Southern version is savoury, not sweet: no sugar.

items.prepNote: melted, plus extra for the pan

content.text: Heat the skillet and mix the batter
Heat the oven to 220°C. Grease the cast-iron skillet well with butter. Put it in the oven for 10 minutes to heat through.
Put {{polenta}} of polenta and {{plain-flour}} of plain flour in a large bowl. Add {{baking-powder}} of baking powder, the bicarb of soda, and {{salt-table}} of salt. Stir to combine.
Whisk together {{buttermilk}} of buttermilk, the 2 beaten eggs, and {{unsalted-butter}} of melted butter in a separate bowl. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined.

Carefully pour the batter into the hot skillet. It will sizzle as it hits the pan. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Rest in the pan for 10 minutes before cutting into wedges.

items.cause: Skillet not hot enough when the batter went in.
items.fix: The skillet must be smoking hot before the batter goes in. 10 minutes in a 220°C oven is the minimum.

items.cause: Overbaked, or too much cornmeal to flour ratio.
items.fix: Check at 20 minutes. The cornbread is done when a skewer comes out clean. It should feel firm but not hard.

items.cause: Old leavening agents, or batter overmixed.
items.fix: Check that both the baking powder and bicarbonate are fresh. Mix until just combined: lumps are fine.

content.text: Northern sweet cornbread adds 30 g of sugar and is softer and more cake-like. Jalapeño cornbread stirs two finely chopped jalapeños and 50 g of grated cheddar into the batter. Skillet cornbread with bacon fat instead of butter and a handful of cooked crumbled bacon stirred into the batter is a Southern classic.

Southern cornbread is one of the defining foods of the American South, eaten alongside almost everything from beans to gumbo to collard greens. The unsweetened version is associated with the Deep South; the sweetened Northern version is a different dish entirely. The dispute between the two is a genuine cultural fault line in American food culture.
